pages.page_title: w sprawie potencjalnych konfliktów interesów w Komisji Kodyfikacyjnej Prawa Cywilnego
pages.capture_answer: Signatory: Arkadiusz Myrcha, Sekretarz Stanu, for the Ministry of Justice. Date: Warszawa, 29 września 2025 r., reference BK-VII.0520.299.2025. The reply answers interpellation no. 11127 by MPs Anna Gembicka and Jarosław Sachajka on conflicts of interest in the Civil Law Codification Commission (KKPC). Amounts are per role, not per person: a monthly flat-rate remuneration of 10 000 zł for the chair, 8 500 zł for the deputy chair and 3 500 zł for a member, set in § 13 ust. 1 of the regulation (the 2002 Council of Ministers regulation, cited as Dz.U. z 2024 r. poz. 1447). The reply does not say how the chair is appointed. The only named individual payment is Marek Miller's waived remuneration. The reply gives no cost totals and no 2025 figures, and KKUSiP is not mentioned. Krystian Markiewicz, Maciej Taborowski and Marcin Dziurda do not appear, and no member list is given. The reply states there is no legal duty for members to declare whom they serve, and that members must withdraw where there is a conflict-of-interest risk. The reply refers to the Prime Minister and the Minister of Justice by office only; it does not name Donald Tusk or Waldemar Żurek. None of the other listed actors or NGOs appear.

followup_urls.why: Ministry page where, per the reply, Commission plenary-session information is published from 27 November 2024. The PDF text runs 'kodyfikacyjnaprawa' together and ends in a footnote digit, so the exact address is unverified. Not fetched.

The markiewicz -> uni_silesia edge is supported: Markiewicz is 'profesor nadzwyczajny Uniwersytetu Śląskiego', and the centre is a site of the university network. The page does not mention the Constitutional Tribunal or Markiewicz's TK status. Tomasz Nawrocki (sociologist, member) is not linked on the page to President Karol Nawrocki. pages.capture_answer: No TVP S.A. supervisory-board member is named, so nothing on Maciej Taborowski's role, start date, monthly pay, legal basis or appointer appears in this letter. It is the Ministry of Culture's reply to interpellation 15635 from MP Barbara Bartuś of 3 March 2026 on the legal and financial situation of TVP SA and Polskie Radio SA in liquidation. Signatory: Maciej Wróbel, 'Sekretarz Stanu', signing on behalf of the Minister of Culture and National Heritage. No date line is visible in the returned text; the latest date in it is the 2026 TVP grant figure, stated as of 28 February 2026. Captured as claims: the 27 December 2023 extraordinary general meeting resolutions to liquidate TVP and Polskie Radio, the ministry's statement that a planned broadcasting-law amendment would change how company bodies are selected, and the TVP subsidies for 2024 to 2026. Polskie Radio subsidy figures are also in the letter but are not tied to any listed actor, so they were not captured.

pages.page_title: Ujawniamy kulisy odwołania zastępcy RPO. Partyjny deal w instytucji, która powinna być niezależna
pages.capture_answer: Deputy removed: dr hab. Adam Krzywoń, deputy Ombudsman. The new Ombudsman is Sylwia Gregorczyk-Abram. The only party named in the visible text is Lewica. The standfirst says Anna Maria Żukowska of Lewica confirms that dr Michał Peno will take the post on the club's recommendation, and the body has the line 'Lewica musi mieć swojego rzecznika'. KO, Polska 2050, PSL and PiS are not named in the visible text. Peno is described as a former Unia Pracy politician who has so far worked in the justice ministry; no appointment date is given for him. Dates: the RPO office announced on 9 października that Friday was Krzywoń's last working day, and the article is dated 11 października 2026. The 'party deal' is alleged by unnamed RPO office staff, who also say Gregorczyk-Abram was to tell Krzywoń she was dismissing him. The office says it did not dismiss him and that they parted by mutual agreement, and that personnel decisions rest on merit. Gregorczyk-Abram denies the nomination is political. OKO.press says the office's reply conflicts with its findings. The rest of the article is paywalled.

pages.page_title: New members of Venice Commission appointed - Ministry of Foreign Affairs Republic of Poland - Gov.pl website
pages.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs Republic of Poland
pages.capture_answer: Answered from the page. Dated 02.03.2026, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs page says the government announced the nomination of Prof. Wojciech Sadurski and Prof. Monika Florczak-Wątor as new Polish representatives to the Venice Commission, and that the newly appointed experts 'will serve as members', so neither is described as a substitute. The steps it gives are national government nomination and approval by the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe for a four-year term; the page does not say that approval was given to these two. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said the decision was taken 'together with the Ministry of Justice'. Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek is quoted on the candidates' standards and independence. The page gives no party for Sikorski or Żurek. Sadurski is a professor of law at the University of Sydney and at the Centre for Europe at the University of Warsaw. Florczak-Wątor is a professor at the Jagiellonian University, and her work 'focuses on' the functioning of the Constitutional Tribunal, but the page names no Tribunal post, contract or fee for her. The page names no ISP, Batory Foundation, Osiatyński Archive or KOD tie for either nominee, and no fee or payment. Prof. Hanna Suchocka is named as a previous Polish representative. The ISP and IACL items were not linked from this page and were not read.

pages.capture_answer: The Senate passed the two TK bills on Wednesday 31 July 2024 (new TK act and the implementing act): 51 for, 30 against, 0 abstentions. The Senate rejected the PiS senators' motion to reject the Sejm's changes and adopted most amendments, mainly editorial. Because of the amendments both bills return to the Sejm. Senate committees and rapporteurs are not named on the page.

pages.page_title: Burza wokół Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. Co się stało w piątek wieczorem?
pages.capture_answer: Friday 30 Oct 2026, about 18:00: the TK website posted notice of a one-month break in the duties of TK president Bogdan Święczkowski and vice-president Bartłomiej Sochański. The order was issued by judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, who as the most senior judge by service took over running the TK. Earlier she asked the police to act at the TK seat, where demonstrators have gathered against Maciej Berek's swearing-in. Komenda Stołeczna Policji (KSP) said it took statutory actions; officers entered the TK grounds but not the building; KSP said it conducts no actions in the seat. No SOP (Służba Ochrony Państwa) or TK guard action is mentioned. No TK chancellery official, spokesperson or police commander is named, and no dismissals are reported. Same evening, Prosecutor General Waldemar Żurek announced five immunity motions (224 pages total per his post): four against Święczkowski, one against Sochański, all handed to the most senior judge. Not in this article: the Sejm transcript, the July police action, or any prosecutor closure decision.

pages.page_title: POLAND – Country visit for the forthcoming Opinion on the Laws on the Constitutional Tribunal
pages.page_date: 14 - 15 October 2024 (visit dates in page header); no publication date shown
pages.capture_answer: A Venice Commission notice of a delegation's country visit to Warsaw on 14-15 October 2024, to prepare an Opinion on the Laws on the Constitutional Tribunal and draft constitutional amendments concerning the TK. The Minister of Justice of Poland requested the Opinion on 4 September 2024; the minister is not named. Bodies and people met, as listed: the Minister of Justice; Members of Parliament from the governing coalition and the opposition (no chamber and no names given); the Constitutional Tribunal; the Chancellery of the President; the Deputy Commissioner for Human Rights (the page does not use 'Ombudsman'); a former President of the Constitutional Tribunal (unnamed); and civil society organisations (unnamed). Not on the page: any rapporteur or Secretariat name, the CDL-AD(2024)035 number, the Sejm or Senate by name, Iustitia, Themis, Batory or HFHR, or any core actor (Tusk, Wawrykiewicz, Żurek, Bodnar, Święczkowski, Nawrocki, or the eight TK judges). No fee or payment is mentioned. The draft Opinion was to go to the 141st Plenary Session on 6-7 December 2024 for adoption.

pages.publisher: The National Tribune (Australia), republishing an OHCHR press release
pages.capture_answer: Republished OHCHR press release dated 29 May 2026 on the end-of-visit findings of UN Special Rapporteur on the independence of judges and lawyers, Margaret Satterthwaite. Visit dates: not stated; the page says only 'At the end of an official visit to Poland'. Bodies and people met: none named. The page says 'everyone I met during my visit' and 'all stakeholders' but names no Ministry of Justice, TK, KRS, judges' association or NGO as met. Constitutional Tribunal: only 'a shuttered tribunal', in a list of obstacles, with the tribunal not named. Oath refusals: 'an unsubstantiated denial of appointment oaths' appears in the same list, but the page does not name the President or any official as the person who denied the oaths; 'an unexplained veto' is also unattributed. New body: 'This new Council of the Judiciary offers hope, and should start work immediately' (not named as KRS). Report: 'my report in June 2027' (the body receiving it is not named). None of the core actors (Tusk, Wawrykiewicz, Żurek, Bodnar, Święczkowski, Nawrocki, or the eight TK judges) is named on the page.

pages.capture_answer: CV of Anna Adamska-Gallant as a judge of the European Court of Human Rights 'as from 16 December 2024'. PACE election date: not stated on the CV, the composition page or the judges list (the list gives only the year, '2024 – Anna ADAMSKA-GALLANT'). Term: the composition page says judges 'are elected for a non-renewable term of nine years'; her own end date is not stated (speculation claim: about December 2033). Nominating state: Poland, as shown on the composition page; the government that proposed her is not named. That page also says judges 'hear cases as individuals and do not represent that State'. NGO or association ties on the CV: National Board member of the Polish Judges Association 'Iustitia', 2009-2011, the only association listed; no Themis, Free Courts, Batory or HFHR tie is listed. Government or ministry post: none listed. Courts: judicial assessor, Gdańsk labour court (2001-2002); judicial assessor, Biała Podlaska misdemeanour division (2002-2004); judge, Lublin criminal division (2004-2013). International posts: International Judge, Kosovo* Court of First Instance, criminal division (2013-2015) and International Judge, Supreme Court, criminal chamber (2015-2018). Expertise France: 'Key International Expert' on the Judicial Reform of the EU Pravo Justice in Ukraine (2018-2024). Other: private criminal-law practice (2021-2024); lecturer at the University of Wrocław Faculty of Law, Administration and Economics (2021-2024); lecturer for trainee lawyers on the European Convention on Human Rights (2023-2024). Education entries are not captured as posts.

pages.capture_answer: This is the coalition's January 2026 contribution, not a 2026 PDF report. It names seven organisations and Krzysztof Izdebski as submitter. Constitutional Tribunal content: the NCJ amendment ruling of 20 Nov 2025 (government has not published it); CJEU C-448/23 (18 Dec 2025) on TK 'double judges' and the appointment of the TK President; the 2025 budget omitted TK judges' pay. No 2026 Sejm-elected judges and no oath dispute appear in the full text. No funder, donor or grant is acknowledged. 'Annex I' is not referenced. Donald Tusk (p.52) is cited for 'opinions of leading legal experts' on 2023 media dismissals; the opinions were not disclosed and no fee is named. Adam Bodnar (p.53) pledged at a 2024 Warsaw anti-SLAPP conference to abolish criminal defamation. Note: the 2016 TK judgment (K 13/16) concerns the National Broadcasting Council (KRRiT), not the NCJ.

pages.capture_answer: On 15 May 2026 the deputy Ombudsman Adam Krzywoń (not Gregorczyk-Abram, who is not named on the page) received the PACE Monitoring Committee delegation at the BRPO office in Warsaw. Members named: Christophe Brico and Didier Marie, rapporteur group; the page gives no countries. Maciej Kruk, director of the BRPO Presidium and International Cooperation Team, accompanied the receiving deputy. Topics: the situation of the Constitutional Tribunal and the status of judges appointed via the KRS after 2018, plus the legal consequences of challenging individual rulings over bench composition. The visit is part of a PACE monitoring procedure opened against Poland in 2020. No funder, sponsor, or organiser is named.

pages.capture_answer: Justice Minister Bodnar appointed Kraków Regional Court judge Waldemar Żurek deputy director of the National School of Judiciary and Public Prosecution (KSSiP) for organisational affairs on Friday 7 June 2024; he heads the Director's Office and permanently deputises for the Director. The same day Kraków judge Izabela Fountoukidis became second deputy director; further deputies were to come from the prosecution service. Piotr Girdwoyń is named as the new KSSiP director. Career note: first an Iustitia member, then Themis vice-president and board member; KRS member 2010-2018 (two terms); Kraków Regional Court spokesperson for over 14 years. Pay not stated.

pages.page_title: Zwycięstwo 15 sędziów z listy praworządnościowej w wyborach do KRS. Radzik dostał tylko 14 głosów!
pages.capture_answer: Judges' assemblies across Poland gave opinions on 60 KRS candidates, each judge casting up to 15 votes; turnout about 60%. All 15 places went to the 'rule-of-law list': Zawistowski 4201, Jefimko 3587, Frąckowiak 3583, Bąk-Lasota 3537, Zawiślak 3536, Mierzejewska 3474, Kierszka 3405, Łuczaj 3394, Żołnierczuk-Dec 3386, Buchajczuk (Iustitia vice-president) 3382, Starosta 3363, Cilulko 3358, Wrzesińska-Nowacka 3355, Donhoffner-Grodzicka (Themis board) 3297, Kobylińska-Bortkiewicz 3289. Ziobro-era candidates: Radzik 14, Piebiak 39, Schab 34, Dudzicz 33, Zdun 54, Czubik 66, Dalkowska 86. The Sejm was to elect the judge-members soon, as the neo-KRS term ended in May 2026.

pages.page_title: Nowi sędziowie KRS wybrani przez Sejm. Wśród nich współpracownik Ziobry
pages.capture_answer: On Friday 15 May 2026 the Sejm elected 15 judge-members of the KRS (235 for, 18 against, 5 abstaining; 3/5 majority of 155; PiS MPs did not vote, citing a TK injunction of 12 May). 13 were named by the ruling coalition's clubs after the judges' assemblies' opinion vote, in which judges backed by associations including Iustitia and Themis won most support. The other two: Łukasz Piebiak (PiS pick, ex-deputy justice minister under Ziobro) and Łukasz Zawadzki (Konfederacja pick), both linked to Stowarzyszenie Prawnicy dla Polski. Of the assemblies' top 15, Sławomir Cilulko and Themis board member Beata Donhoffner-Grodzicka are not on the elected list.

pages.capture_answer: Print 253 (the 2024 deputies' TK bill) was filed with a cover letter dated 6 Mar 2024, the day of the Sejm's TK resolution. It had 136 MP signatures. Four MPs were authorised to represent the movers: Kamila Gasiuk-Pihowicz, Sławomir Ćwik, Michał Pyrzyk and Katarzyna Ueberhan. Signatories already on the map: Czarzasty, Myrcha, Paszyk, Hennig-Kloska. Committee chair Śliz also signed. Rapporteur Jaskulski did not sign, and neither did Tusk, Giertych, Budka or Adam Bodnar. No drafting credit (e.g. Batory) appears in the parts read. The page states no clubs.

pages.capture_answer: The Sejm elected the six on 13 Mar 2026 (53rd sitting, day 3). Votes: Markiewicz 236-187-4, Taborowski 237-185-4, Korwin-Piotrowska 236-185-4, Dziurda 237-182-6, Szostek 237-185-4, Bentkowska 236-186-4. The six were put forward by the ruling coalition after a recommendation from the Sejm Presidium. PiS candidates: Skwarzyński (positive committee recommendation, not elected) and Kotowski (negative; the only candidate absent from the hearing). A TK resolution was adopted the day before: 235 for (KO, PSL-TD, Lewica, Centrum, Polska 2050), 197 against; PiS moved to reject it. The article names no movers for the resolution and gives no print numbers or committee vote counts.

pages.capture_answer: Primary statement from the National Prosecutor's Office. On 21 Apr 2026 it opened an investigation into the non-admission of four TK judges elected by the Sejm on 13 Mar 2026. The case has two threads: (a) suspected aiding of the President's failure to fulfil his duties, i.e. not receiving the oaths (art. 18 §3 with art. 231 §1); (b) suspected failure of duty by public officials employed at the TK, who did not give the judges working conditions, pay, cases or employment formalities (art. 231 §1 and art. 218 §1a with art. 11 §2). The basis was a verification proceeding under Prosecutor General Waldemar Żurek's order of 13 Apr 2026, plus a criminal notification filed by TK judges Magdalena Bentkowska and Dariusz Szostek. Signed by prosecutor Anna Adamiak, press spokesperson of the Prosecutor General. No suspect is named.

followup_urls.why: Related PK statement on a notification by TK judges, found in search. May give the case number, the unit and the prosecutors.

pages.capture_answer: Account by Czesław Mroczek, Secretary of State at MSWiA, in the Sejm on 31 Jul 2026. Police acted on a report that two TK judges due at a planned TK General Assembly were not let into the building. They contacted the prosecutor's office at once, and officers and a prosecutor went to the TK only to establish the facts. The TK chancellery director and the TK guard commandant said they were carrying out the TK President's written order not to admit the judges. At the prosecutor's request they handed over a copy, and the judges complied. The prosecutor announced witness summonses and had police send the documentation to the National Prosecutor's Office. The TK President asked the Chief Commander of Police for the legal basis, and the Chief Commander replied.

followup_urls.why: Preceding item in the same session, probably the MP's question this answer responds to (seen in search, not read).
